findings.title: argcov's own docstring never documents its `cfg` or `exempt` parameters in the form its own scan requires
locations: quote: "argcov(cfg; exempt = (hit -> false)) -> (hits, population, skipped)" … "`exempt(hit)` is the ledger's `[exemption.match]` predicate"
findings.description: `Reflection.argcov` is the engine behind RULE.DOC.ARGCOV/SCAN.ARGCOV: every signature parameter must appear in the docstring body as a bare code span `` `p` `` or a span carrying its default `` `p = ...` ``. Its own docstring (Reflection.jl:154-165, shown on Reflection.md) never mentions `cfg` as a code span anywhere, and mentions `exempt` only as `` `exempt(hit)` `` — a call expression, which is neither the bare-name nor the with-default form the code's own regex accepts (`Regex("`" * q * "`")` or `Regex("`" * q * "\\s*=[^`]*`")`). I replicated the exact regex logic from Reflection.jl against the literal docstring text and both `cfg` and `exempt` come back undocumented. `argcov`'s own arg-count/keyword combination (1 positional + 1 keyword) does not qualify for the ARGS_THRESHOLD prose exemption either, since that exemption requires `isempty(kw)`, and `exempt` is a keyword — so this docstring is a real trigger, not a legitimate skip. The rendered deviations.md for this package lists no declared exemptions ("(none)"), so this is not a ledger-covered deviation.
findings.resolution_hint: Add an explicit arguments clause naming `cfg` (the validated config) and `exempt` as a bare span or `exempt = ...`-style span, e.g. "The arguments are `cfg`, the validated config, and `exempt`, the ledger's per-trigger predicate (default always-false)."

findings.title: "hats" (a declared package term of art) used on the landing page with no definition or link
locations: docs/src/index.md:17 — "A consumer carries a `.gbg/` directory: one config file, one exemption ledger, its domain hats, its"
findings.description: "hat" is one of this package's own declared terms of art — `src/CLI/Init.jl:128` writes `"terms" => tool ? ["consumer", "instrument", "round", "lane", "hat", "anchor", "gate", "pin", "managed file", "ledger"]`, matching the lane brief's list verbatim. "hats" is used exactly once across the whole audited surface, at index.md:17 ("its domain hats"), with no clause explaining what a hat is and no `@ref` link to any page that does (the glossary entry lives only in the rendered policy, `.gbg/policy/glossary.md`, which is not part of the docs site). A cold reader of the landing page has no way to learn what a "domain hat" is.
findings.resolution_hint: Add a short clause ("its domain hats — the check-consistency panel's personas —") or link to Rounds/Install/a glossary page on first use.

findings.title: "lane" (a declared package term of art) used throughout the rounds guide with no definition
locations: docs/src/guide/rounds.md:7 — "The CLI writes its marker `ROUND.toml`; the lane agents write their lane files"
docs/src/guide/rounds.md:17-19, 36 — "3. **Lanes** — the printed `Workflow` call; each lane writes `findings/NN-<lane>.json` first."
findings.description: "lane" is likewise one of the package's declared terms of art (`src/CLI/Init.jl:128`). It is used seven times across rounds.md (lines 7, 16, 17, 18, 19, 36) purely operationally ("lane files", "lane 00-scans", "a DEAD lane") but is never given a defining clause or an `@ref` link stating what a lane conceptually is (per the glossary, "one agent of an instrument … a surface or territory"). A reader coming to this page cold (its stated purpose is to explain what a round is) learns the file-naming mechanics of lanes but not the concept itself.
findings.resolution_hint: Add one clause at first use, e.g. "the lane agents — one per surface or territory the instrument covers — write their lane files".
